newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Ashton to start final Merlin study.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Ashton to start final Merlin study.

text.p: Ashton Mining Ltd said on Friday it would start an engineering and final feasibility study for the Merlin diamond joint venture project in the Northern Territory.
"A decision on mine development, subject to satisfactory feasibility results, is expected by May 1997, with first production possible in first quarter 1998," Ashton said.
Ashton said the decision had been taken after receiving the valuations for diamonds recovered from recently completed bulk sampling and concentrate processing in its Perth Laboratory.
The Merlin diamonds receovered to date are descibed as being 35 percent gem quality, with the remainder near gem quality, with virtually no boart, it said.
It said the highest valuation was from the Launful pipe at Merlin with a result of US$140 per carat.

"This is a significant step towards the establishment of Australia's second hardrock diamond mine and is a reward for the joint venture's commitment to diamond exploration in the Northern Territory," Ashton chief executive John Robinson said in a statement.
The Merlin project has identified 12 diamond-bearing pipes to date. Ashton owns 32.93 percent of Merlin, Australian Diamond (ADEX) owns 44.50 percent and Aberfoyle 22.57 percent.
Ashton is the project manager with a net beneficial interest in the venture of 67.5 percent. Ashton has a 77.6 percent stake in ADEX and earlier announced it would make a full takeover bid.
Ashton, which is 46.95 percent owned by Malaysia Mining Corp Bhd, is offering A$1.40 for each ADEX share it does not already own.

At 11.50 p.m. (0050 GMT), Ashton shares were one cent higher at A$1.99, while ADEX was untraded on Friday, but the shares rose sharply on Thursday, up 27 cents, or 26.2 percent, at A$1.30 on light volume.
